title: Install a Python package when pip says externally-managed-environment
summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12 block pip from installing packages into the system Python. Create a separate virtual environment for the package, then install it there. The system Python stays untouched.

aliases.text: how to pip install on ubuntu 24.04
pip externally managed environment что делать
как установить python пакет через pip на ubuntu

prerequisites: A terminal window on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12 or Linux Mint 22
Your user account can use sudo (it asks for your password)

steps.explain: Check which system you have. Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 12 show their version here, and this card applies to them.
steps.expect: A line like PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 24.04 LTS" or PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)".

steps.explain: Check the Python version. Any Python 3 works here; the venv step below uses the same python3 command.
steps.expect: Python 3.12.x on Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.11.x on Debian 12.

steps.explain: Look for the marker file that tells pip the system Python is managed by apt. If the file is listed, pip will refuse to install into the system Python.
steps.expect: A path like /usr/lib/python3.12/EXTERNALLY-MANAGED (python3.11 on Debian 12). If you see No such file, this card's error does not apply to your system.

steps.explain: Refresh the list of available packages so that the next install finds the latest version.
steps.expect: Lines starting with Hit, Get or Reading package lists, and no error at the end.

steps.explain: Install the tool that creates virtual environments. A virtual environment is a private folder with its own Python packages, so nothing goes into the system Python.
steps.expect: The last lines say Setting up python3-venv, and the command returns to the prompt.

steps.explain: Create a virtual environment in a folder of your choice. Use a folder you own, such as one in your home directory.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder to create for the virtual environment. It must not exist yet.

steps.expect: No output. The folder appears with a bin directory inside.

steps.explain: Install the package into the virtual environment with its own pip. The system Python is not changed.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: The folder created in the previous step.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the Python package on PyPI.

steps.expect: A line that starts with Successfully installed and names the package.

alternatives.explain: Same install, run through the Python of the virtual environment. Use this if the pip command above is not found.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: The folder created in the previous step.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the Python package on PyPI.

alternatives.expect: A line that starts with Successfully installed and names the package.

verify.expect: A block that starts with Name: followed by the package name, and a Version line.

rollback.explain: Remove the package from the virtual environment.
Delete the whole virtual environment folder. Only use the folder you created in this card, and check its name first.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: The virtual environment folder you created. Double-check the name: this deletes it.

rollback.expect: No output. The folder is gone.

rollback.explain: Remove the virtual environment tool if you do not need it. Other programs do not depend on it.
rollback.expect: The line Removing python3-venv appears, and the command returns to the prompt.

warnings: Do not use pip install --break-system-packages or sudo pip install. They write into the system Python, and apt tools that depend on it can break.
Packages in a virtual environment work only for programs started with that environment's python or pip. Use <VENV_DIR>/bin/python to run your code.
The rm -r command deletes the folder and everything in it. Check that the path is the venv you created.
The sudo commands ask for your password and install system packages. Run them only on your own computer.
